resumen: Held against a wall with your thighs parallel to the floor, without moving. There is no range of motion: the work is holding it.
ejecucion: With your back to a wall, rest your whole back on it and walk your feet forward.
Slide down until your knees are at 90° and your thighs parallel to the floor.
Your feet end up under your knees, hip-width apart.
Hold for the set time, breathing normally, without clenching your teeth.
If your knees complain, go down less: slightly higher thighs still count.
matices: In the cited meta-analysis of 270 trials and nearly 16,000 people, isometric exercise lowered resting blood pressure the most (−8.2/−4.0 mmHg), ahead of aerobic and classic resistance training, and this wall squat was the single most effective mode for systolic pressure. That is an effect on blood pressure, not a way to gain strength or muscle: squats with a range of motion serve better for that.

fuentes.titulo: Exercise training and resting blood pressure: a large-scale pairwise and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
fuentes.autor: Edwards et al., Br J Sports Med, 2023
